item.title: The Hate for Miami Runs Strong (and Across Continents): My Unique Experience with the 2010 Sun Bowl
item.description: EL PASO, TX - DECEMBER 30: Running back Cierre Wood #20 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish runs for a touchdown against the Miami Hurricanes during the Hyundai Sun Bowl at Sun Bowl on December 30, 2010 in El Paso, Texas. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahh the Sun Bowl. The first bowl game in the Brian Kelly era for the Notre Dame Fighting Irish, and technically the chance for the Irish to win back-to-back bowl games in my entire lifetime (2008 was the Hawaii Bowl, and 2009 was the last year of Weis with no bowl game – see, it’s not like bowl opt-outs for the Irish are new). The Not-So-Sun Bowl Many people will remember the Sun Bowl for how hilariously it was not sunny nor warm. It had snowed in El Paso before the game, and it was freezing outside. It also pitted Notre Dame against Miami in the first matchup of the two teams in 20 years. The last time the two teams played was in 1990 in South Bend when the Irish won, and there was still the Catholics Vs Convicts moniker relevant with the rivalry. This matchup got announced, and our household became ecstatic. My dad found someone online who recreated the Catholics Vs Convicts shirt, and that was one of my Christmas presents that year. I had only heard stories of the hatred for Miami because of 1986-1990, but never even came close to experiencing it truly. Our king, Tommy Rees A Different Place for the Game We were excited for the bowl matchup, but myself and my parents had a different thought process. The game was early afternoon on New Years’ Eve – a chance to ring in the final day of 2010 with some Irish football. However, we were across the pond in London. I was in the marching band in high school and was one of the drum majors (if titles mean anything to you). The high school band takes a trip every other year, and that year was the New Years’ Day parade in London – an amazing experience! I distinctly remember, though, that with my dad’s nuts fandom and excitement for the rivalry to be “back”, we were at a NYE party/gathering of sorts at our hotel for all of the bands participating in the parade. But, my dad was trying to go to the hotel bar to see if the London TVs even had American CBS on the channels. I think somehow he was able to find the game and watch a bit of it. I was in London, but was still focused on what was happening in El Paso, TX and ruminating on the fact I couldn’t watch the game live. Remember TiVo? We’re glad we had it When we got back stateside, I remember we got home and went to bed that night. But, the first thing we did in the next morning, the day before I went back to school from that Christmas break, was fire up the ol TiVo and watch the full game. We knew the score, but we diligently watched every play. I look back on this because we are crazy ND fans, but I think we wanted to see with our own eyes and see proof that the Irish could dominate Miami once again, since it had been so long. We have [Santiago] Castro as an alternative to [Donyell] Malen but in midfield we’re short. Hopefully it’s just a phase. We’ve spent the last seven games on a knife edge but we’ve always had players who were ready and able to recover quickly. Rodrigo Mora is fine. The 17 players we have are all ready. Hopefully we’ll get the others back after the international break, but in the meantime this is a tough week.” That was Gian Piero’s response when asked about the difficulties Roma currently face in the injury departmen t. item.title: West Ham were right to be ruthless with Nuno, but are they right about Scott Parker?
item.description: “I am always under pressure, every day,” Nuno Espirito Santo said in the wake of Saturday’s 3-1 loss to West Brom. Not anymore, he’s not. An optimistic outlook on his removal as West Ham coach is that it offers respite. Respite from that pressure, which has never truly waned in his 13 months in charge. It might seem a ruthless move by the east London club to fire him “so early” into the season, but West Ham were right to be ruthless. But let’s not forget that the Championship season is already a quarter of the way done, and true ruthlessness would have entailed sacking the Portuguese over the summer, after he failed to stop West Ham from plummeting into the Championship – despite taking over from Graham Potter in late September. The former Nottingham Forest and Tottenham coach never truly steadied the ship in the Premier League . There was barely even a new-manager bounce to be buoyant about, never a moment when Hammers fans could breathe easily, and even the seas of the second tier (which he navigated so well by winning the league with Wolves in 2017/18) proved too choppy this time around. That is not to say his West Ham side have been disastrous this season, but with immediate promotion essential from a financial standpoint – and in order to keep the best of this squad together – six wins, four draws, and three losses were never going to instal adequate confidence. Eighth place, one quarter of the way through the season, is too risky a spot. It is okay to drop points intermittently in such a long, arduous campaign, but the move to sack Nuno was motivated by West Ham’s fear of those points practically spilling out underneath them, like marbles. Nuno’s bubble has burst at West Ham (PA) It would, of course, have been nice for fans to see a move not motivated by fear; perhaps a change in the summer would have felt harsh, but it would have been proactive, and there is an argument it would have felt encouraging in a different sense. On the topic of encouragement, West Ham’s free-scoring start to the season was a refreshing sight after recent times at London Stadium, and they remain the highest-scoring team in the division, but their goal difference has already been matched. And for Nuno, 52, and his players, the issue has not just been conceding too many goals, but also the timing of those errors: they have conceded first in nine out of their 16 games in all competitions. That has signaled a concerning fragility, which has tasked West Ham with fighting back far too often – in a season when many expected them to lead from the front, no less. Admittedly, there was a degree of naivety to this sentiment. Over the summer, it was all to easy for neutral fans to assume that West Ham would walk the Championship, when supporters of the east London club knew how misguided these claims were. item.title: “Jerry Jones Is Now Drinking Milk Instead of Vodka”: Rob Parker Claims Cowboys GM Has Lost His Fire, Tolerating Ineptitude of Brian Schottenheimer’s Team
item.description: Aug 7, 2026; Canton, OH, USA; Pro Football Hall of Fame president Jim Porter (left), NFL commissioner Roger Goodell (center) and Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones at the Pro Football Hall of Fame. © Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys broke an unwanted record on Sunday, losing for the first time at home after leading by 14 points against the Arizona Cardinals. The Cardinals also maintained their unbeaten streak at AT&T Stadium, logging their fifth win there since the venue opened in 2009. As several critics called out the team’s effort in the monumental collapse, radio host Rob Parker took the opportunity to blast Cowboys owner Jerry Jones for losing his competitive fire. During his daily radio show on Fox Sports Radio, Parker said : “Jerry should hang it up. Jerry should just go home. No, no, seriously. Because, like, there used to be a fire in him that would not be acceptable, but just to sit there and go, what a shame. And they lost to Tampa Bay. They lost, like, the division is sitting there. And I brought that, you know, we talked about that a couple of weeks ago. But Jerry’s reaction to me, Jerry is now drinking milk now instead of vodka.” The Cowboys avoided disaster early in the game when running back Javonte Williams fumbled the ball in the end zone, but backup tight end James Mitchell recovered it, putting six points on the board. However, in the fourth quarter, quarterback Gardner Minshew II was unstoppable, throwing three touchdowns to Tyler Allgeier, Trey McBride, and Michael Wilson, respectively, to complete an 11-point halftime comeback. Mike LaFleur Refuses to Name Starting QB For Week 9 While Gardner Minshew II led the team to a historic comeback after the team subbed out Jacoby Brissett amid a disappointing performance, head coach Mike LaFleur refused to reveal who will start at QB in Week 9 against the Seahawks. During his postgame conference, LaFleur said : “I know what the story is going to be and so does (Jacoby).” LaFleur also spoke on the team’s mentality to keep fighting after a difficult first half, saying: “You got to applaud the fellas in this locker room for fighting, the defense for getting a stop, and then the offense obviously getting us into range when we needed to there in overtime. We go have a chance to redeem ourselves and knock it down. I think that’s a testament to the guys that we have in this locker room, which is the most cliché thing you can say, but it’s not cliché when it’s true, right?” After improving to 3-5, the Cardinals will face the Seattle Seahawks, who lost to the Chicago Bears in a blowout on Monday Night Football. item.title: Takeaways from Maryland men’s basketball’s season-opening 96-67 win over Bucknell
item.description: Maryland men’s basketball had a difficult time getting off the starting line in its season opener against Bucknell, ceding the lead on two occasions. But after launching a 21-5 run to close out the first half, the Terps never took their feet off the gas. Maryland overcame a sloppy start and took control in the second half of Monday night’s contest to cruise to a 96-67 victory over the Bison. Returning guard Andre Mills led the way with 22 points as the leader of five different Terps who scored in the double digits. The win didn’t come without its issues, however, as Maryland struggled to shoot accurately from the 3-point and free-throw lines. Here are three takeaways from the first win of the Terps’ 2026-27 campaign. Bench talent was on full display Talk of Maryland’s improved depth heading into this season was one of the biggest reasons why many critics predicted the team would take one of the largest jumps in the nation. The bench proved those predictions right against Bucknell, combining for 35 crucial points. The biggest contributor off the bench was undoubtedly freshman guard Kaden House, who contributed 14 points in 18 minutes on 4-of-9 shooting. His breakout performance was highlighted by a monstrous drive and slam eight minutes into the second half that sent the crowd into pandemonium. Kaden House nearly took off the rim with that poster, outdoing DJ Wagner's dunk earlier in the half. He's been a star off the bench in his college debut. pic.twitter.com/AVRWCuOSam — Testudo Times (@testudotimes) November 3, 2026 Robert Jennings III and Baba Oladotun also scored seven points, albeit with varying levels of efficiency. Jennings made both of his field goal attempts — including a surprising 3-point swish from the wing — while Oladotun struggled to get going in his 16 minutes of playing time, going 25% from the charity stripe and failing to score until 27 minutes into the game. “Any 17-year-old that’s supposed to be in high school, no matter who the opponent is, who’s playing in his hometown state in game number one, he is going to be sped up,” head coach Buzz Williams said. “We had some 23-year-olds that were sped up.” The game gave fans a glimpse of 12 of the 15 available Terps, with Maban Jabriel, Alex K’Medehouto and an injured Guillermo Del Pino riding the bench. As Maryland continues to face weaker non-conference opponents in the coming weeks, Williams will iron out which of his players will see minutes during the Big Ten slate. This included a beautiful grab-and-go play from Mills at the close of the first half that created momentum heading into the locker room. item.title: Milwaukee Bucks’ seldom-used center labeled the ‘difference-maker’ by Taylor Jenkins vs. Minnesota Timberwolves
item.description: Beyond giving Brayden Burries his first NBA start, Taylor Jenkins also made the bold move of playing Jericho Sims during the Milwaukee Bucks ‘ 112-100 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday evening. Sims last suited up in the team’s opening loss to the Washington Wizards. Sims replaced Kyle Kuzma as the Bucks trailed 25-16 with less than four minutes left in the first quarter, and the 28-year-old center provided quality minutes on defense, as the Timberwolves scored only four points before he was subbed out. Jericho Sims energized the Milwaukee Bucks during his short stint Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Milwaukee Bucks center Jericho Sims (00) dribbles the ball during the third quarter against the Charlotte Hornets at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images Jericho Sims played only 15 minutes for the Milwaukee Bucks yesterday. The Texas product had only two rebounds and one assist and didn’t shoot at all, but head coach Taylor Jenkins called him a difference-maker. “He brought great energy, great life,” Jenkins said of Sims. “He’s constantly staying ready. Love how he’s been approaching day-to-day, the play groups, just game plan discipline. We worked on that this morning. He had a great session this morning. Obviously, at a moment’s notice, he got called into action. I liked how he was switching, controlling the ball, even though the stat line – he wasn’t scoring – it was all the ancillary things he was doing that gave us a spark and allowed us to continue to keep that game within striking distance in the first half.” Jericho Sims on finding his niche within the Milwaukee Bucks Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Bones Hyland (8) works around Milwaukee Bucks center Jericho Sims (00) in the first quarter at Target Center. The big part of tonight was before the game, in our pregame, we were talking about getting ‘kills’ (defensive stops) and trying to get three in a row. Maybe that didn’t work out all the time, but just having the mentality to try to get multiple stops in a row helped us,” Sims told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. item.title: Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown Risks NFL Fine After Unflagged Hit That Concussed Cardinals Player
item.description: Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown has recorded 8 combined tackles and one forced fumble across three games this season, while Arizona Cardinals running back Zonovan “Bam” Knight has tallied 168 rushing yards on 28 carries and 43 receiving yards over eight games. However, a controversial incident changed the focus of the game. Arizona defeated Dallas 33-30. The hit resulted in a fumble, but the referees called no penalty. This missed call led to intense criticism far beyond the field. Cardinals suffer injury blow as DeMarvion Overshown escapes penalty flag The collision came late in the first half, with Dallas recovering the fumble and Arizona losing another back after Love’s injury. Dec 9, 2024; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (13) reacts after making a tackle against the Cincinnati Bengals in the first quarter at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tim Heitman-Imagn Images Marshall Green criticized the decision : “So Cam Skattebo gets flagged for running low and protecting the ball, but DeMarvion Overshown is allowed to create helmet-to-helmet contact, hurt a defenseless player, by leading with the head and no call. Gotta love the NFL.” Analysts and reporters on the broadcast noted that Overshown led with his shoulder and that the play included head-to-head contact. Knight stayed down for several minutes before trainers helped him to the tunnel. The Cardinals later ruled him out with a concussion. The hit produced Dallas’ crucial first-half turnover and helped the Cowboys protect a lead heading into the locker room. It did not stop Arizona’s comeback. Tyler Allgeier stepped up significantly in the backfield to help fill the void left by the injured running backs. Knight had three carries for 17 rushing yards and one catch for one yard before the injury. This marked Arizona’s second major backfield loss of the game, following rookie Jeremiyah Love’s earlier ankle injury. The NFL rulebook lists impermissible use of the helmet under Rule 12, Section 2, Article 10. The rule covers forcible helmet contact, but the league has not announced whether it will review or discipline Overshown for this play. Dallas fell from 3-4 to 3-5 after surrendering a 14-point lead. Arizona finished with 467 total yards, including 191 scrimmage yards from Allgeier. Although no penalty was flagged during the game, the sequence will likely be evaluated by the league under standard post-game disciplinary procedures. item.title: Emotional Lions Locker Room Scene Unfolds as Dan Campbell and Jared Goff Address Jack Campbell Situation
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has recorded 42 solo tackles and six total pressures across the 2026 season, anchoring the team’s defense despite a slower statistical start compared to his previous campaign. The aftermath of the Lions’ hard-fought 19–15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings quickly shifted focus away from the scoreboard as uncertainty loomed over the locker room. Dan Campbell leads Lions in prayer for injured Jack Campbell In an emotional postgame address, head coach Dan Campbell and quarterback Jared Goff turned the team’s focus from a hard-fought victory to the sobering reality of their teammate’s injury. Sep 28, 2023; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers guard Zach Tom (50) moves in against Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (46) during the first quarter at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark Hoffman-USA TODAY Sports In a postgame video, Dan Campbell told the team , “I do not have any more information on Jack. We don’t know anything else at this point. So here’s what I want to do, man. We’re going to take a knee. Now, I want to pray for Jack, okay, and let’s keep him in our thoughts and prayers. That’s a hell of a win, man. You guys break it down. I love you boys. Stick together. I know that’s tough with Jack. Stick together, lean on each other, all right? Good job. Win on three. One, two, three. Win.” Campbell was hurt making a tackle on the first play of the fourth quarter. He stayed face down on the field before medical personnel placed him on a backboard and moved him to a cart. The Lions said he was alert and breathing before he went to the hospital. Detroit later said Campbell was resting at the hospital and that preliminary indications were positive. The team did not provide a diagnosis or return timetable. item.title: Why did Dmitri Voronkov's role shrink for Columbus Blue Jackets?
item.description: Dmitri Voronkov has played for three NHL head coaches since joining the Blue Jackets in 2023, and each had the same reaction to seeing him in full gear for the first time. More: Columbus Blue Jackets leaning on young core with free agency looming Heads shook, shoulders hunched, eyes beamed and their smiles resembled those of kids set free in a candy shop, daydreaming as NHL coaches often do, about Voronkov's potential as a 6-foot-5, 230-pound unicorn on skates . Standing in full gear, which adds roughly two inches and a few more pounds, the 26-year old Russian power forward can darken a hallway and light up expectations at the same time. It doesn't take much to see visions of Voronkov squishing people like bugs, pummeling them with Christmas ham fists or scoring 20-plus goals while making life a living hell for goalies. That's about the extent of it, though. What's happened in Voronkov's first four NHL seasons is that coaches start off excited to skate him in a top role before steadily reducing his ice time once they see that his physical dominance only shows up in fits and starts. And that's where things stand with Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness , who still hasn't seen Voronkov's full impact since taking over the bench from Dean Evason last season. “He has to be physical, absolutely," Bowness said. "You don’t want him turning away from anybody. When he’s out there, his presence should be felt because he is a big man, right?” Too often, it's not. Voronkov, a pending restricted free agent, too often skates with a cloak of invisibility. That must change whether he's playing for Bowness with the Blue Jackets or another NHL coach during a fresh start. Going into the Blue Jackets' game against the Colorado Avalanche on Oct. 3 at Nationwide Arena, Voronkov has played in just eight of 12 games without scoring a goal. His only points are off two assists, he's been replaced as a net-front option on power plays by Matthew Knies and Valeri Nichushkin and his ice time is down to 10:36 per game after a drop from the second line to the fourth. Bowness is willing to let Voronkov work his way back up the lineup into a prominent role, but he'll be watched closely for specific traits the coaching staff needs to see. “It’s being physical and [staying] at the same level the whole shift," Bowness said. "There can’t be a drop-off. That’s always been the concern. He goes hard. He’s got to be able to forecheck and backcheck at the same tempo, as opposed to forecheck and lose it on the backcheck." Whether that's dictated more by Voronkov's physical fitness or his preferred style of play — skill over brawn — remains the biggest unknown in that regard. The most accurate answer might cover both options, which isn't an easy fix. Voronkov has been told to improve his fitness the past three summers, and results have varied. item.title: Ravens get even more bad news at quarterback position
item.description: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports The Baltimore Ravens lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. Unfortunately for Baltimore, the bad news at quarterback didn’t stop there. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who is in line to start Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars, is now dealing with an ankle injury of his own. He was listed as limited on Monday, though head coach Jesse Minter said he still expects Fagnano to have a chance to play. Ravens’ Quarterback Woes Jackson, who had just returned from a high ankle sprain that cost him three games, injured his right thumb on his first throw of Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills. He will need surgery and is headed to injured reserve, and Minter said the injury could “potentially” end his season. Huntley took over for Jackson after his injury, but suffered a toe injury in the second quarter. That forced Fagnano into his NFL debut, and he went 10-of-21 for 91 yards with an interception as the Bills rolled to a 36-10 win. The loss dropped the Ravens to 4-4. The team has reportedly shown interest in trading for a veteran quarterback , and on Monday, Baltimore signed Austin Reed to its practice squad. Fagnano went undrafted after a college career at Maine and UConn, where he threw for 3,448 yards and 28 touchdowns with just one interception last season. He earned the Ravens’ third-string job with a strong preseason. ‘Fighting Through a Couple Things’ While Fagnano seems to be the team’s best option at quarterback, it doesn’t sound like he’s exactly healthy, either. Fagnano was hit low by Bills defensive lineman Ed Oliver on Sunday, but he played through it and finished the game. On Monday, he was listed as a limited participant in the Ravens’ walkthrough and Minter said that Fagnano is dealing with some issues. That said, he expects the rookie to be available. “To Joe’s credit, he’s kind of fighting through a couple things he’s dealing with,” Minter said, via the Ravens’ official website . “But expect him to have a chance to play on Thursday.” Minter didn’t have an update on Huntley’s timeline, saying the team is “working through that as well.” With a short week and limited options, the Ravens will likely be counting on Fagnano to tough it out against the Jaguars. The Huskers were flying high early in the season, but their recent skid has seen the head coach’s children being subjected to some nasty rhetoric. Rhule shared the story of what his 13-year-old daughter dealt with, making it clear just how much the situation ended up impacting him. “A guy walked up to my 13-year-old daughter and was like, ‘F*** you and f*** your dad.’ I’m not going to keep coaching if it means my kids grow up s****** up,” Rhule said . “I’m not coaching for the guy that attacked my daughter, I’m coaching for the people in the boat. For the people who are listening to the game while they’re on a combine. We are going to fight for those people. But please don’t ever question how hard these kids are working or how hard these coaches are working or how hard I’m working.” It’s not surprising that fans can get emotional at times, but saying something like that to a child is well beyond the pale. Nebraska is lucky that Rhule seems committed to staying. This type of incident genuinely could have been enough to get a coach to move on from the team. item.description: Shedeur Sanders remains in the backup role with the Cleveland Browns. Getty Shedeur Sanders remains in the backup role with the Cleveland Browns. Getty Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders Getty The Cleveland Browns could accept a bargain return for Shedeur Sanders as they weigh the future of their crowded quarterback room. ESPN Cleveland’s Tony Grossi believes general manager Andrew Berry might move Sanders for less than a fifth-round pick — the round in which Cleveland selected him in 2025. In a Nov. 2 column for The Land on Demand, Grossi examined Berry’s history of trading quarterbacks and questioned whether even a modest return could help thin out their crowded room of passers. “Any Berry trade analysis would be remiss without discussing the quarterback position. In seven seasons as Browns GM, Berry has traded Joe Flacco (and a sixth-round pick) for a fifth; Kenny Pickett for a fifth; Dorian Thompson-Robinson as a throw-in in acquiring Pickett; and Josh Dobbs (and a seventh) for a fifth,” Grossi said. “So the questions are: Would anybody offer a fifth for Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel, and would Berry be willing to move either quarterback? My opinion is that Berry will not receive a fifth for either QB, but he might be willing to part with Sanders for less than a fifth. Grossi sees little reason for the Browns to carry four quarterbacks past the trade deadline, particularly when he expects them to pursue a long-term answer early in next year’s draft. “It simply makes no sense for the Browns to keep four quarterbacks through the 2026 season when they surely will be in the market for a QB high in the 2027 draft.” Shedeur Sanders Has Had Little Chance to Build His Case Getty Sanders has spent his second season waiting behind Deshaun Watson, with few opportunities to show Cleveland or potential trade partners his progress. item.title: FIFA to share documents related to World Cup private investment plan
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino pictured in Vietnam in August (Nhac NGUYEN) FIFA will allow members of its ruling Council to view "key documents" related to the aborted project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, a source close to world football's governing body told AFP on Tuesday. "FIFA has informed the members of its Council, including all the vice-presidents, that they will have access to key documents in relation to FIFA Forward Enterprise," the source told AFP, referring to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's FFE proposal. Members of the Council -- a total of 37 people including Infantino and eight FIFA vice-presidents -- were informed on Monday in a letter sent by FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom that they must come forward "in the next two weeks" if they want to see the documents "in person and in specific conditions". The documents can be consulted at the headquarters of world football's governing body in Zurich, Switzerland, the source added. The move came as a November 2 deadline set by European governing body UEFA to answer a series of questions related to the FFE proposal passed on Monday. UEFA has led the opposition to the project, which was revealed in late July and would have seen FIFA open up its premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of an uproar, but UEFA has gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of "criminal mismanagement" against the FIFA president in Switzerland. Following a FIFA Council meeting on October 15, UEFA general secretary Theodore Theodoridis sent a letter to Grafstrom with a list of over 40 questions and requests for information related to FFE. It also raised other issues such as the decision to award a FIFA Peace Prize to Trump and the decision to suspend a red card shown to United States player Folarin Balogun at the World Cup following an intervention by the US President. FIFA did not respond to UEFA before the deadline, arguing that this was "impractical". Infantino is standing for re-election as FIFA president next March. The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is November 18, but UEFA has so far not been able to find a credible challenger to put forward. Infantino was handed a major boost when the Asian Football Confederation announced on October 23 that it was backing him for re-election. CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani was mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian has announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of the North American confederation, meaning he is unlikely to challenge Infantino. Ramon Vega, the former Tottenham Hotspur, Celtic and Switzerland defender, has stated a willingness to stand but it remains to be seen if he will get the necessary support. kn/lh/as/gj

item.title: Two Real Madrid players who have benefited from Valverde’s right-back role
item.description: Two Real Madrid players who have benefited from Valverde’s right-back role Jose Mourinho’s astute skill in balancing out profiles on the field has been key in Real Madrid’s resurgence, particularly in the last month. Los Blancos did not start the new season strongly, and the midfield appeared to be a mess early on. Mourinho’s idea of a Federico Valverde-Aurelien Tchouameni double pivot, in particular, did not work out on the field. The manager then found an innovative solution to add creativity while also retaining Valverde and Tchouameni’s impact on the game. He sacrificed a natural right back and placed the captain in that position, and moved one of Arda Guler or Bernardo Silva to the newly opened midfield slot to enhance the creative output. Both stars benefit Silva’s importance has grown in recent weeks. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The decision to move Valverde to right-back opened the doors for Guler and Bernardo to solidify their place in the starting XI. While the former was having a good season regardless, the latter was relatively struggling up until that point. Since the new system began, both players have flourished and are now two of Mourinho’s most trusted personnel on the field. Additionally, both players bring completely different profiles to the field, giving the manager tactical versatility. The Portuguese star brings a sense of calm and control to the middle of the park, and with his experience also comes an extraordinary ability to understand spaces and movements. Guler, on the other hand, stands out for his unpredictability , creativity and ability to create imbalances – something very different from Bernardo. Both players, in fact, have also shown that they can operate in tandem. Where there are winners, there are losers Trent Alexander-Arnold appears to be losing his spot. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) While Guler and Bernardo Silva have both benefited and grown into the team’s regular dynamics in midfield, the manoeuvre to bring Valverde to right back has displaced the team’s natural defenders. Just last summer, Los Blancos roped in Trent Alexander-Arnold amid much hype with a lot of expectations placed on the former Liverpool star. This summer, they went on and signed Denzel Dumfries as well, taking on a second world-class right-back. Now, however, both players appear to have no chance of starting in the big games as Valverde has settled into that role comfortably, and they thus emerge as the players on the losing end of the deal.

item.title: Barcelona to observe minute of silence before Aston Villa clash for Jesus de Miguel and Toledo train accident victims
item.description: Barcelona to observe minute of silence before Aston Villa clash for Jesus de Miguel and Toledo train accident victims Barcelona will observe a minute of silence before their Champions League encounter against Aston Villa at the Spotify Camp Nou on Tuesday evening, paying tribute to CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel and the victims of the deadly train accident in Urda, Toledo. The Portuguese head coach managed Scottish giants Rangers for a brief spell in 2017 and has since managed in a variety of places, from Brazil to Saudi Arabia and most recently Mexico. (Photo by Gregory Fisher/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In Monday’s ACC Action, #14 Miami fell to #1 Florida, 77-67, Louisville beat Chattanooga, 84-70, Clemson handled Stetson, 85-72, Syracuse dismissed New Haven, 74-58, Pitt took care of Rider, 95-57, NC State knocked off Campbell, 83-64, SMU chased off Southern, 85-72, Cal hammered Adams State, 115-86, Wake flew away from Maryland Eastern Shore, 83-62, Florida State trashed Florida A&M, 113-69, and Stanford grounded Eastern Washington, 74-65. Oh, and UNC just did get by Western Carolina, 80-72. Last time out, UNC needed overtime to beat Charlotte. We’re starting to understand why Dean Smith never wanted to play in-state teams. UNC needed a late 13-2 run to pull this one out, partly because the Catamounts controlled the boards, 41-32, and doubled UNC on the offensive glass, 13-7. Next up for UNC is Wofford, and there’s some history there, too. Miami gave Florida a good game, and definitely hung around, but every time they got too close, Florida would push the lead back to around 10 points. But Miami learned they can compete with the #1 team in the country. Next time might be different. #11 Louisville was cruising against Chattanooga but took its foot off the gas in the last 10 minutes or so. All five starters finished in double figures. Obinna Ekezie, so impressive when Louisville played at Kansas, took only one shot here (and hit it). Former UNC guard Seth Trimble started and played well, scoring 13. NC State did well in Justin Gainey’s coaching debut, building a 65-30 lead before coasting to the win. Campbell shot just 37 percent overall and 23 percent from deep, while State shot 54 percent overall, and 44 percent from behind the line. Campbell is not on the same level, so let’s see how the Pack does against a better team. That probably won’t occur until the ACC/SEC Challenge, when State faces Gainey’s old boss, Tennessee’s Rick Barnes. We have a lot of respect for Clemson under Brad Brownell. That guy knows what he’s doing. Stetson is not really a powerhouse, so who knows what this means. However, Ace Buckner had 20 points.
